郡.meaning: A <part>mister</part> in a top hat rides round the edge of the land, planting a <part>pennant</part> on every hill he passes. When he gets back to where he started, every village inside the ring of flags shares one sheriff, one fair and one map: a new <kanji>county</kanji>.
郡.on: Big <sound>Gun</sound>ther wins the sheriff's job by carrying all the flags at once.
郡.kun: Along the river bank, he marks the county line with <sound>co</sound>ld <sound>ree</sound>ds.

勾.meaning: A yoga teacher tries to <part>wrap</part> her arm round her own back, bending her <part>elbow</part> further and further until she's tied in a bow. Her students copy, and soon every arm in the room is hooked and twisted. Today's lesson: how to <kanji>be bent</kanji>.
勾.on: Afterwards nobody can straighten up enough to lick an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne.
勾.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>lm flock of <sound>gee</sound>se waddles in and untangles them with their curved necks: a hook.

阜.meaning: A <part>snowman</part> in a flat park wants a view. <part>Ten</part> pigeons take pity on him and each bring one beakful of earth a day. By spring he stands, a bit melted but very proud, on top of a little <kanji>mound</kanji>.
阜.on: He keeps warm with a rolled-up <sound>fu</sound>ton for a scarf.

曹.meaning: Two clerks share an office that is just <part>one</part> plank balanced on a single <part>pole</part>, like a see-saw desk, out under the blazing <part>sun</part>. Each time one stamps a form, the other's end flies up. Wobbly, but it's an <kanji>office</kanji>.
曹.on: They scrub the ink off their hands with a bar of <sound>so</sound>ap from the stream.

佳.meaning: A mole hangs his tiny hat on a <part>coat hook</part> by his door and shows off his new home: a <part>double mound</part>, one hill of soil neatly piled on another, with a balcony. The other moles gasp. A two-storey molehill is <kanji>excellent</kanji>.
佳.on: His neighbour, a big orange <sound>ca</sound>rp, pops up from the pond to applaud.

藤.meaning: A <part>bodybuilder</part> trains on the <part>grass</part> under the <part>moon</part>, lifting weights beneath a vine that drapes long purple flower bunches over his bench. Every rep shakes loose a shower of petals. His favourite gym is under the <kanji>wisteria</kanji>.
藤.on: One petal lands on his big <sound>toe</sound> and he squeaks.
藤.kun: He naps on a <sound>fu</sound>ton there, then drives home in his <sound>jee</sound>p, petals in his hair.

葛.meaning: A gardener puts up a <part>sunshade</part> over a patch of <part>grass</part> and goes in for lunch. When she comes back, a twisting vine has climbed the shade, swallowed it whole and is reaching for her chair. She digs it out and finds a fat, starchy white root: <kanji>arrowroot</kanji>.
葛.on: She grinds the root to flour and fries a crispy <sound>katsu</sound> in it.
葛.kun: Her <sound>coo</sound>k squeezes yu<sound>zu</sound> over the top and serves it on the vine.
